title: Malicious Claude Code extension builds in Cursor attempted persistent SSH backdoors
summary: Cursor confirms modified Anthropic.claude-code builds 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows in its marketplace. They collected host details and attempted persistent SSH access; these builds were not developed by Anthropic. Cursor's November 13 investigation says an exposed Fireworks access key allowed theft of historical non-Privacy Mode agent traces. Credentials in the traces enabled access to internal SaaS tools and subsequently the marketplace cache.

severity.rationale: Cursor confirms attackers stole credentials from historical agent traces and used stolen credentials to distribute malicious extension builds. Vendor-confirmed exploitation reaching credentials warrants a 24-hour response, even though the distribution window has closed and the attacker server is offline.

affected.product: Anthropic.claude-code artifacts from Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace
affected.note: Modified macOS and Windows builds 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 distributed on October 29, 2026. Version numbers alone do not distinguish these artifacts from official builds.
Limited stored non-Privacy Mode traces, mostly from 2025; Cursor directly notified affected customers. No client version threshold applies.

exposure: The extension compromise is limited to the identified Cursor marketplace artifacts. Cursor reports no evidence that official distributions or other extension versions were affected. The separate trace-data exposure affected notified non-Privacy Mode users; Cursor says Privacy Mode prompts and code, the Cursor app, official updates and live traffic were unaffected.

params.instructions: Compare extension installation history and VSIX hashes with the Cursor notice; inspect its SSH and persistence indicators. An absent SSH key alone does not prove no payload executed. Check vendor notifications for exposed trace data and specific credentials requiring rotation.

remediation.details: Remove the malicious extension and its standalone persistence, unauthorized SSH key and tunnel processes. Isolate systems with execution evidence, assess rebuilding, and rotate accessible credentials and sessions from a trusted system.
remediation.risk: High. Isolation, persistence removal and credential rotation can interrupt workflows.

remediation.action: Rotate credentials identified in vendor notifications
remediation.details: Team administrators notified of trace-related exposure should rotate the specific keys listed by Cursor. Extension remediation remains necessary for the malicious artifacts.

verification: Verify extension and persistence removal using the vendor indicators and review telemetry for payload execution.
Confirm all credentials listed in the vendor exposure notice have been rotated.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Added vendor-confirmed trace credential exposure and the link to marketplace tampering from the November 13 investigation, with notification-based remediation.

Recorded vendor-confirmed exploitation involving stolen trace credentials and malicious extension distribution; raised severity to critical with a 24-hour response and clarified the separate exposure scopes.

exploitation.note: Cursor confirms theft of historical traces containing credentials, subsequent unauthorized SaaS access and malicious extension distribution. The October 29 notice reports payload execution and persistence; the November 13 update links the stages of the incident.
